title: Suicidality and routine blood parameters in gender-incongruent individuals: an exploratory investigation of biological correlates and their clinical assessment
summary: Gender-incongruent individuals are still underrepresented in research, although they may have an increased risk of suicidal thoughts and suicidal behavior. At the same time, some studies suggest that certain blood parameters may be associated with suicidality. The aim of this study is to assess the severity of suicidal symptoms in gender-incongruent individuals and to explore whether these symptoms are associated with routinely collected blood parameters. In addition, the study examines whether suicidality documented in routine clinical records corresponds to suicidality assessed by a standardized questionnaire. This is a monocentric cross-sectional observational study. Data will be collected once during a routine follow-up visit in the endocrinology outpatient clinic using a questionnaire on suicidality, while laboratory values and other routine clinical data will be retrospectively extracted from the electronic medical record.

interventions.name: Adult gender-incongruent individuals presenting as part of routine clinical care at the endocrinology outpatient clinic of Frankfurt University Hospital and providing informed consent for study participation will be included.
